ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Path + feed phase

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how path difference and feed phase combine to produce constructive or destructive interference.

For two elements separated by d along the array axis, the relative observation phase is ψ = kd cos θ + β, where k = 2π/λ and β is the applied feed phase.

Their field sum is AF = 1 + eʲψ. The coherent-peak-normalized power is |AF/2|² = (1 + cos ψ)/2. Constructive addition occurs when ψ is a multiple of 2π, and cancellation occurs at an odd multiple of π.

Broadside means θ = 90°, where the projected path difference vanishes. Endfire means looking along the element axis; the spacing and phase must be considered together to distinguish its two directions.

Example

With d = λ/4 and β = −90°, the +axis has ψ = 0 and adds constructively. The opposite axis has ψ = −180° and cancels.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. For two isotropic elements with d = λ/2 and β = 180°, do the two axial directions behave differently?

    Insert cos θ = +1 and −1 into ψ.

    Both axes add: their phases are 2π and 0. These settings alone do not give a one-sided endfire pattern for the stated two-element isotropic model.
